token_csprng.evidence: server.js:117 jwt.sign({ userId }, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '30d' }); server.js:11 const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET || ...
token_csprng.note: Tokens are JWTs signed with a key read from the JWT_SECRET environment variable. If that variable is unset, the code uses a hardcoded literal instead (see no_hardcoded_secret).

no_hardcoded_secret.note: Hardcoded fallback signing key. start.sh does not set JWT_SECRET, so this key is used by default and anyone who knows it can forge tokens.

token_expiry.evidence: server.js:142 jwt.sign({ userId: user.id }, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: '30d' })
token_expiry.note: 30-day expiry, checked by jwt.verify at server.js:79.

logout_revokes.note: Logout only clears the token in the browser. There is no logout endpoint, session table or denylist on the server, so a token stays valid until it expires.

xss_safe_render.note: escapeHtml (index.html:869-873) works by reading div.innerHTML, which escapes &, < and > but not double quotes. A title containing " can break out of the value attribute and inject event-handler attributes when the note is opened for editing. Other places use escapeHtml or textContent, and error messages go through innerHTML (index.html:619).

security_headers.note: No helmet and no res.setHeader for Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options or X-Frame-Options.
